diagnosis: N2 BREACH. V5 Sweep's general emission path (S-e, sweep_emit_general) wrote every lemma of the sub-solver's replayed refutation with EVERY LITERAL NEGATED, so drat-trim/cake_lpr could not derive the clause the line claims. Root cause: the sub-solver and the kernel share the `2*v | negated` literal encoding, and `sweep_detect_seed` encodes into it with the parity carried through unchanged (`sub_lit(sub_of_var[var_of(l)], negated(l))`), but BOTH decode sites -- `sweep_capture_dir`'s local `to_lit` and `sweep_emit_general`'s inline decode -- spelled the inverse as `make_lit(vars[sub_var_of(sl)], (sl & 1u) == 0)`, i.e. `negated = sl is POSITIVE`. WHY IT WAS SILENT for the whole S-e increment: the two decode sites agreed with each other, so (a) the negated target of direction 1 is exactly direction 2's binary and `sweep_apply`'s `is_pair` check accepts the pair in either order, (b) both binaries are still added, so F is CORRECT and the solver's verdict is right, (c) `sweep_emit_general`'s own final-step check compares the emitted target against a target read off the same inverted decode, so it passes. Only a checker sees it, and only when a negated lemma reaches the core: drat-trim checks backward and prunes lemmas the refutation does not need, so DefaultPolicy x DRAT (the standing per-commit leg) was green; the standing native-LRAT leg runs --random-policy, where Sweep emitted nothing at all on these cases -- a vacuous arm ([[ab-arm-identical-artefacts]]). The uncovered quadrant, --random-policy x native DRAT, rejects 1 in 63 UNSAT fuzz cases. Fixed 2026-08-05 by routing both decodes through one `sweep_kernel_lit(vars, sl)` that carries the parity.
